label: Vector Calculus
notes: Open the chapter. Vector calculus turns analytic structure into differential operators on fields. The deck follows PDF pages 26 through 36 and covers derivatives and the Jacobian, gradient and directional derivative, divergence and curl, the chain rule, and the integral theorems that connect local and global behavior in geometric deep learning.

label: Derivatives and the Jacobian
notes: Define the derivative of a multivariate map as the best linear approximation, encoded by the Jacobian matrix of partial derivatives. Differentiability means the linear map approximates the function to first order. Backpropagation is exactly repeated application of the Jacobian through composed layers, so this object is foundational to learning.

label: Gradient and Directional Derivative
notes: Specialize to scalar fields. The gradient is the vector of partials pointing in the direction of steepest ascent; the directional derivative projects it onto a chosen direction. Gradient descent follows the negative gradient, making this the engine of optimization in every neural network.

label: Divergence and Curl
notes: Introduce divergence and curl on vector fields. Divergence measures net outflow at a point; curl measures local rotation. The Laplacian is divergence of the gradient and reappears throughout spectral theory and diffusion on graphs and manifolds, linking calculus to later chapters.

label: Chain Rule and Integral Theorems
notes: State the multivariate chain rule as composition of Jacobians, then the integral theorems of Green, Stokes, and Gauss that relate a field on a region to its behavior on the boundary. These theorems generalize to differential forms and underpin conservation laws and message-passing aggregation.

label: Recap
notes: Close the chapter. The Jacobian linearizes maps, the gradient drives optimization, divergence and curl describe flow and rotation, and the integral theorems tie local derivatives to global boundary behavior. Chapter 04 lifts this calculus onto manifolds via differential geometry.
